macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS AFTER RE-EXAMINATION, flagged loudly because +15.9% protein sits just past the ~15% tripwire. The re-examination the rule demands was done line by line: the main protein is NOT each-assumed - it is the source's own 3.5-cup cooked measure through the estate's standing 140 g/cup densities row (the same row chicken-bacon-ranch validated to 0.1% against ITS source) and the DB's 3:4 cooked-to-raw factor, and every other line is weight- or measure-anchored. Calories agree within 1.9%, which a wrong portion would not allow. The gap decomposes into named product-form differences, not portions: (1) our part-skim mozzarella row (23.6 P/100 g) vs their evident whole-milk basis, (2) our 1/3-fat cream cheese (disclosed substitution: +0.3 P, -3.5 F) vs their full-fat, (3) their calculator's lighter cooked-chicken cup (their 34.19 F with 29.85 P is the fattier-dairy signature; our fat runs 4.6 g lighter for the same reason). Direction is safe for the run's claims: if anything the card understates nothing - protein is computed from labels, and the calorie band verdict is identical on either side of every named difference.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 443.0 cal in [400, 650] PASS (43 above the floor; the floor margin survives every named product-form difference - swapping in full-fat cream cheese would RAISE it to ~470); carbs 9.9 g <= 35 PASS. No optional lines.
